prompt: Review this anchor as its assigned subagent. Enumerate ALL requirements, qualifications, edge cases and scenarios. Inspect all supplied implementation and test fragments and trace each aspect to implementation behavior and actual test assertions or justified TODO/N/A evidence. Passing tests and associations alone are insufficient. Follow helpers and capture every additional source dependency with cargo meta review read ANCHOR PATH [selector] before completing the report. Explain prerequisites for justified TODO tests; do not claim deferred behavior is implemented. Distinguish source inspection from commands actually executed. Write a JSON report containing reviewer, report, and requested_edits. Leave requested_edits empty only when every aspect is accounted for and no edits are needed. Otherwise list concrete changes, including missing tests or justified TODO tests with prerequisite comments. Run cargo meta review record ANCHOR REPORT_FILE to finish. After edits or stale-input rejection, run cargo meta review start ANCHOR and review the fresh inputs. The gate fails until a current report with no requested edits is recorded. Dependency capture is agent-declared.
coordinator_instructions:
Follow sage-review-checklist for only the assigned anchor. Begin fresh review using cargo meta review start ANCHOR --instructions /tmp/ci-anchor-review-instructions.txt. Inspect current claim, implementation, complete tests, and capture dependencies through review read. Independently assess current evidence; do not transplant old approvals. Preserve justified TODO/N/A entries honestly. Record a complete claim-specific report. Coordinate all source edits with root BEFORE editing, to avoid invalidating concurrent reviews. Prefer reporting concrete necessary changes for root to batch; do not add unrelated evidence. You own only your assigned validation directory and unique /tmp report. Distinguish source inspection from tests executed. Do not commit.
Root centrally runs relevant suites. Do not repeat full suites for a source-only review unless investigating a specific concern. Report source assessment honestly without claiming execution. This does not waive regression reproduction for suspected bugs.

Acceptance merges the record and specification changes together; unfinished
implementation or tests remain explicit TODO entries. Subsequent implementation
replaces those entries with code and evidence. Completing an RFD does not require
copying its rules into Design, because the normative changes were already
expressed there.

# Maintaining This Book
Update the specification with the code in the same change. Read the Design
[overview](../design/README.md), the affected crate's modeled entities, and any
relevant RFD before editing. The book is the source of truth for Sage's current
design; the generated anchor inventory reports implementation and test coverage.
## What belongs where
- **Meta** specifies this book, `.sage`, evidence extraction, checking, and review.
- **Tenets** explains principles and motivation without specification anchors.
- **Crates** starts with a handwritten reading map. Its generated `.sage`
chapters contain architecture, operations, and claims beside their owning
entities. Focused Markdown chapters can explain cross-cutting behavior and
substantial semantic algorithms.
- **Anchors** is generated. Do not maintain copies of claims, source excerpts,
tests, or status tables there.
- **RFDs** record motivation, alternatives, affected specification pages, and
implementation sequencing. Their branch includes the normative Design diff.
Completed records remain useful history; they do not define active rules.
- **The User's Guide** explains how to use tools. Worked examples explain
concrete scenarios without replacing the specification or its evidence.
There is no separate numbered Architecture Decisions registry or manually
maintained implementation-status catalog. Preserve reasoning in an existing RFD
or an explicitly retrospective record. Plans and ordering belong in RFDs;
per-rule implementation, test coverage, and limitations belong with the
source associations displayed on anchor pages.
## Writing a rule
Give each independently testable claim its own anchor. Follow the
[Anchor tenets](../design/tenets.md#anchor-tenets) when deciding what belongs
together. Prefix the opening paragraph with a local marker, without a blank
line before its text:
```text
{anchor}`cache_invocations`
Every annotated invocation is checked, including cached requests.
In `design/meta/contracts.md` this names
`meta.contracts.cache_invocations`. A chapter namespace derives from its path
relative to `design/`, with hyphens normalized to underscores, extensions
removed, and `README` denoting its directory. Headings and sidebar order do
not affect identity. Use the same definition marker inside `.sage` triple-quoted
prose; put the claim beside its owning declaration or method.
A `{spec}` role with a full rule name references the rule without defining it.
Code examples are not definitions. See [anchor mechanics](../design/meta/anchors.md)
for exact syntax, content boundaries, and reference validation.
Keep qualifications needed to interpret the guarantee inside the anchor's
content. Multiple paragraphs or an example can explain one guarantee; split
requirements that can be implemented, tested, or changed independently.
The specified content extends until the next definition, any section heading,
a standalone `<!-- end anchor -->`, or the containing document/prose-block end.
The explicit end lets unrelated commentary follow without another heading.
Blank lines retain subsequent paragraphs, lists, tables, and examples in the
claim. The generated views and saved review use that same complete content.
Keep the end marker on its own line outside code and HTML examples; an end
marker without an active anchor is an error. Inspect the extracted claim when
editing nearby prose, and review enlarged inputs through the normal checklist
workflow. The [content-boundary migration](../rfds/sage-contracts/implementation.md#anchor-content-boundaries)
records the implementation and corpus audit.
Move detailed contracts into `.sage` as their owning entities become clear;
introduce more structural syntax when it makes the requirements more precise.
Formalization must preserve existing requirements.
## Implementation and tests
Connect each claim to both implementation and tests:
```rust,ignore
// {anchor}`meta.contracts.cache_invocations`<<
check_invocation(caller, callee)?;
#[test]
#[sage::test(meta.contracts.cache_invocations)]
fn cached_invocation_is_checked() {
// The actual test must visibly exercise and assert the claim.
A point comment without `<<` gives a five-line preview after the marker. A
region explicitly bounds the excerpt. Multiple sites are supported. Ordinary
entries, entries inside `todo`, and entries inside `not_applicable` retain
independent statuses and explanations. Missing entries are errors; they are
not implicitly TODO. Do not introduce a placeholder when meaningful coverage
already exists, or label a passing placeholder as implemented behavior.
Eligible tests use the built-in `#[test]` attribute in a Cargo target with a
standard enabled test harness. Ignored tests do not supply coverage. Source
inventory retains cfg conditions without claiming that those conditions held
or the test executed. Test adequacy review and test execution are separate.
Use `.agents/skills/sage-review-checklist/SKILL.md` when the claim, associated implementation files, or complete
test set changes. Reviewers inspect the exact inputs, including TODO/N/A

explanations. Start each anchor review with `cargo meta review start <anchor>`, capture extra context with `cargo meta review read`, and record its complete report in `validations/<anchor-id>/` through `cargo meta review record <anchor> <report-file>`;

do not rewrite snapshots merely to make CI pass. Approvals cover implementation completeness and test adequacy. Changes to captured source fragments require fresh review; consult the review specification
for the exact snapshot boundary.
## Navigation and generated content
Register handwritten chapters in `SUMMARY.md`, except companion Markdown
guides under `design/crates/<crate>/`: the Crates chapter includes those through
the shared chapter inventory. Keep `.sage` files in that same crate directory
with a `crate.sage` manifest. The preprocessor generates crate subchapters and
anchor pages; do not create Markdown copies of `.sage` sources. CI's orphan
chapter check uses this inventory, including generated chapters, and rejects
Markdown sources that would not be published. Write links to the relevant
source chapters and use direct entity links when pointing to an operation or
value type.
A source badge opens the rule's generated anchor page. Its context link returns
to the precise definition. Moving or renaming a rule requires updating its
implementation/test references and incoming links together. The modeled
entity identity, such as `$sage_ir::symbols::Symbol`, is independent of the
chapter-derived rule name.
The book snapshots Rust source. Rebuild after Rust edits to refresh excerpts.
It works without a running Sage server, and embedded explorers follow the
book's theme. Keep the handwritten Crates landing page concise and link its
subsystem introductions to the owning modeled crates.
The separate `// ANCHOR:` / `// ANCHOR_END:` excerpt convention remains useful
for explanatory worked examples; it does not establish specification coverage.
## Verification
Run the shared check and build the book:
```sh
cargo meta check
mdbook build
With the configured HTML and linkcheck renderers, the rendered site is in
`book/html/`. The Pages workflow publishes that directory and checks that
`index.html` exists there before uploading; publishing `book/` instead nests
the site under `/html/` and leaves the site's root URL returning 404.
The same library check runs in workspace Cargo tests. Run focused behavior tests
for changed claims, format Rust, and build the workspace. Inspect the generated
index and representative source → anchor → source links, including `.sage`
claims. Keep TODO/N/A visible until substantive implementation and evidence
replace them. Remove an old chapter only after accounting for its numbered and
unnumbered requirements and preserving useful rationale and links.
## Inline compilation tests
The [Inline Compilation Tests](../rfds/inline-compile-tests/README.md)
RFD explains keeping source fixtures, annotations, and expectations directly
inside an ordinary `#[sage::test(...)]` Rust test. The
[Design specification](../design/crates/sage_test_harness/compile-tests.md)
describes the API and observation contracts.
For these tests, ERROR/WARN markers and compiler conditions express intended
behavior. Adding or changing one is an assertion change that requires a
semantic explanation. Agents must inspect unexpected diagnostics and decide
whether the implementation or intended test behavior is wrong before changing
markers. Do not add an ERROR marker merely to make a test pass or to permit
snapshot blessing. `UPDATE_EXPECT=1` updates observed representations only
after every annotation and diagnostic match is valid. Review the resulting
diff and rerun with updating disabled.
The saved anchor review includes the complete annotated function, including
its inline macro arguments, source, markers, options, and expectations. The
harness macro's implementation is not part of that snapshot. Keep the relevant
scenario and assertions visible at the call site so a reviewer can evaluate
the claim without expanding the harness.
# Requests for Discussion (RFDs)
RFDs are a way of planning out larger changes. They aren't required but they can be useful.
Open a branch and PR containing both an RFD based on the
[RFD template](TEMPLATE/README.md) and the corresponding changes to the
[Design specification](../design/README.md). The RFD records motivation, goals,
alternatives, and the implementation plan. The Design diff states the proposed
normative behavior in specification paragraphs and `.sage` declarations. This
workflow is itself specified by [the book specification](../design/meta/book.md#meta.book.rfd_changes).
Each RFD is a subdirectory like `rfds/my-rfd/README.md` with a companion
`implementation.md` for tracking steps. Add it to `SUMMARY.md`. RFDs can have
subchapters or other accompanying material.
An unsettled proposal is listed under *Draft* in `SUMMARY.md`. Acceptance moves
it to *Accepted* and makes its implementation plan eligible to begin. Draft
RFDs may record alternatives and proof obligations, but destination design
pages must distinguish their planned mechanisms from built behavior.
Identify independently testable requirements as named **specification anchors**
in the Design chapters changed by the branch. Link the RFD's rationale and
implementation steps to those anchors. Include a high-level overview of the
needed changes, with direct links to the affected Design pages and anchors, so
a reviewer can move from the proposal to each normative change. The book and
anchor system are subject
to the same process: changes to how specifications are named, rendered, or
validated change their own Design rules. See the
[authoring contract](../contributing/maintaining-the-docs.md#writing-a-rule) for
the syntax and current tooling limitations.

If the PR is accepted, the RFD will be merged in. At that point you open implementation PRs based on the RFD until it is completed. Each implementation PR should update the RFD's `implementation.md` to reflect its status.
Before marking the RFD complete, account for every affected specification
anchor through the generated inventory. Record genuinely cross-cutting choices
and feature-local rationale in the RFD itself. If preserving reasoning that
predates an RFD, label the record retrospective; do not invent a past proposal
or acceptance date.
Finally, move it from *Accepted* to *Completed* in SUMMARY.md (the path stays
the same).
The latest version of the overall design is documented in the [Architecture & Design section](../design/README.md) — RFDs describe the journey, architecture pages describe the destination.
